doom.driver: Hoax or bomb threats? What we know about flight disruptions across Europe. Security inspections reveal no explosives as fighter jets escort planes amid Europe's major wave of bomb threats.
doom.blurb: OVER EUROPE, FIGHTERS SHEPHERD THE AIRLINERS HOME
doom.summary: Nobody found a single explosive, yet half of Europe's airspace now comes with a fighter-jet chaperone, which is exactly the point of a hoax done well. Meanwhile, Moscow and Tehran are swapping rocket launchers like trading cards, and America's midterm earthquake has the AI data center boom wondering who paid for all that concrete. Add floods across the South and a NASA telescope dropping out of the sky over Indonesia, and today is less apocalypse than a very long list of loose ends.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: No new frontier leaps today, just an MCP explainer making the rounds among developers.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: The Democratic sweep, data center loan fire sales and an Amsterdam site break-in suggest the AI buildout's political weather has turned.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Russia-Iran military ties deepen as the Iran war drags on and a continental bomb-threat wave rattles European skies.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: No models caught scheming today, which is the most we can ask.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Hoax threats, a falling space telescope and a doomsday cult verdict make for an eerie miscellany.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A remote parking stand at Venice Marco Polo airport on the edge of the lagoon, the morning after the bomb-threat diversion, seen as a night scene with a deep violet sky glowing over flat marshy water. A Wizz Air Airbus A321 with a magenta tail sits isolated on the wet apron in the middle of the frame, its air-stairs still lowered and its cabin door open, every window lit blood orange from within. Tall floodlight masts and a ring of emergency vehicle lights pour wide pools of volcanic orange light up from the tarmac, so the fuselage, the puddles and the ground all glow. Spread across the apron are the signs of the cleared threat: a tracked bomb-disposal robot parked with its arm folded, a bomb-disposal van with its rear doors open, and a stretch of sagging police tape strung between traffic cones, now slack and unguarded. A row of passenger suitcases stands in tidy lines on the concrete, each one inspected and chalk-marked, with a sniffer dog sitting calmly beside its handler. The handler is a whole figure in a dark-blue Carabinieri uniform with a hi-vis vest. A second officer in a padded bomb suit with its visor up walks away toward a waiting van, finished for the night. In the background the Venetian lagoon glints bruised violet and orange, the distant skyline of Venice shows as small lit towers, and a Gripen-grey jet trail fades across the glowing sky. A control tower at the right glows with orange windows. Colors: blood orange and bruised violet, with light from below reaching every surface, wet tarmac reflecting the glow, shadows in violet and maroon, and no cool tones. The mood is angry and menacing, with a hollow silence after the false alarm. Everything is in plain view.

minor: A small stray red tail fin sticks up behind the aircraft's nose on the left. It is probably meant as a distant plane but reads as a leftover shape.
The bomb-disposal van's open rear shows muddy shapes inside that don't clearly read as equipment.
The police tape is a thin, faint line between the cones and is easy to miss.
The dog is small and its shape is a little muddled next to the handler's legs.
The aircraft's landing gear and the air-stairs are slightly blobby up close, but they read fine at phone size.

dawn.driver: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin. A surprising new study suggests that an anti-aging drug could help protect people genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's disease. Researchers found that just four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene variant, with women showing the stronge
dawn.blurb: A PLEASANT FOUR WEEKS FOR THE BRAIN
dawn.summary: Four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved blood flow in the brains of healthy middle-aged adults who carry the APOE4 gene variant, offering an early glimpse of protection that could start long before memory changes appear, with women benefiting most. Out in the dark, Voyager 1 is about to become the first spacecraft ever to sit a full light-day from home, and November's sky brings a supermoon and a close meeting of Mars and Jupiter for everyone else. Closer to the heart, a trial of nearly 5,800 adults found that artery calcium scans can guide statin use just as well as traditional risk scores while sparing many people pills they don't need.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: A short course of low-dose rapamycin boosted brain blood flow in people at genetic risk for Alzheimer's, pointing toward prevention years ahead of symptoms.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: NASA is inviting private companies to pitch ideas for keeping the Hubble Space Telescope working well into the future.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is reaching one light-day from Earth, the farthest any human-made object has traveled.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: After two years of hands-on testing, a reviewer has named the kitchen composters actually worth bringing home, making food recycling easier for households.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: NASA's Swift Observatory was built to last two years and instead spent nearly 22 transforming what we know about black holes and exploding stars before its mission came to a close.

copy_pick.why: It is the only candidate with no bad-news hits, its driver is a real study rather than a sky-watching listicle, and 'A PLEASANT FOUR WEEKS FOR THE BRAIN' fits the understatement directive while 1 and 2 lead with Voyager's light-day milestone, which the 11-04 card already covered.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. GROUND-LEVEL VIEW looking steeply upward from a brick-paved garden path in front of a mid-sized suburban home in Columbia, Missouri, in clear balanced golden-yellow and fresh green daylight with confident, steady warmth. Tall mature maple and sycamore trees fill the upper frame, their leaves bright fresh green with golden-yellow light filtering through. The underside of a wooden pergola, heavy with climbing vines, arches overhead against a pale clear sky. In the middle distance on a raised back porch, seen from below, a woman in her fifties with short silver-brown hair, a yellow cardigan and sturdy jeans stands whole and relaxed at the railing. She smiles calmly and looks out over the garden, holding a mug in one hand. Beside her, her grown daughter in a green sweater leans in and laughs, one arm around her shoulders. Both figures are fully visible and silhouetted against the bright sky. On the porch rail next to them sits a small weekly pill organizer with four rows of little compartments, the first few empty and the rest still full, implying a four-week routine. Below them in the foreground, raised garden beds burst with tomato plants, marigolds and bright green herbs, and a watering can rests on the brick path with droplets catching golden light. A few vine tendrils on the pergola curl into a subtle branching pattern like tiny blood vessels. The mood is quiet, steady, and protective: ordinary healthy life continuing, with the future looking secure. Crisp dithered pixel shading, a limited warm palette of golden yellows, leaf greens, and soft sky blue.

minor: The daughter's face in the green sweater is a smooth, nearly featureless blob, so she doesn't clearly read as laughing. At phone size it is small and passable.
The porch stairs and railing on the left join the deck a bit awkwardly, and the support posts under the deck are muddled.
The pill organizer on the rail is a small colorful block. Its rows of compartments aren't readable, but it works as a small object.
The mother's mug is small and hard to make out against her cardigan.
The pergola beams and vines at the top are dense and tangled. The blood-vessel vine pattern is subtle and just looks like tendrils.
